2026-05-28 Guidance raised to $165–169B and roughly $60B AI; EPS from $12.90 to $17.90 A $27B revenue and $5.00 EPS raise in 90 days
2026-07-01 Redomestication from Delaware to Texas effective Installed a 3% ownership threshold for derivative suits and a charter jury-trial waiver on internal entity claims

The five inflections

  • EMC, September 2016: a PC company becomes an infrastructure company on $45.9B of new debt. Before the merger, ISG was $14,978M at a 7.0% operating margin against CSG's $35,877M, so infrastructure was 29% of the company; two years later ISG was $30,917M at 9.9% with VMware consolidated on top, and consolidated revenue went from $50,911M to $79,040M. Purchase accounting produced GAAP operating losses through FY2019. Dell did not report a positive full-year GAAP operating income until FY2020. Core debt then went from $41,166M to $12,997M over eight fiscal years, and every capital-allocation decision from FY2017 to FY2022 was subordinated to it. The part management's current account omits is that the asset Dell bought was losing share when it arrived: Tom Sweet in December 2018 described storage going through "a 4-year period, essentially, where it was losing share," and Clarke on the same call said "15 out of 16 quarters, 13 quarters in a row."
  • The Class V transaction, December 2018: a listing without an IPO. Dell exchanged the tracking stock for Class C shares or $120 in cash capped at about $14B, funded with $5B of new debt. Basic weighted-average shares went from 217M in FY2017 to 744M by FY2021. The dual-class structure survived: Michael Dell's holders and Silver Lake held approximately 91.7% of voting power on 53.8% of shares as of 2026-03-09.
  • The VMware spin, November 2021: the balance sheet fixed, the margin target abandoned. Core debt declined $13.0B in one fiscal year and investment grade followed; the dividend was initiated the next quarter and has been raised every year since. Dell gave up the unit that produced roughly a third of operating income and all of the recurring software revenue. The approximately 12% consolidated operating-margin target set in September 2018 for the FY2023 range was structurally unreachable afterwards — FY2023 was 5.6% GAAP and 8.4% non-GAAP — and it was never restated, withdrawn or bridged. Toni Sacconaghi put the objection on the record at the time: "It's extremely rare that a company divests a faster-growing, higher-margin, more recurring business and preserves one that is less on all of those dimensions." Post-spin revenue went from $101,197M in FY2022 to $95,567M in FY2025, a −1.9% compound rate against a 3%–4% framework, and only the AI year rescued the four-year figure to 2.9%, still below the framework midpoint.
  • The FY2024 bust: the sharpest revenue decline in company history, and the earnings held. Revenue went from $102,301M to $88,425M, down 13.6%, and CSG from a $61,464M peak to $48,916M. Guidance issued on 2023-03-02 was revenue down 15% at the midpoint and EPS of $5.30 ± $0.30. Revenue landed at −13.6% and non-GAAP EPS at $7.13, 35% above the guided midpoint; GAAP operating income declined only 6% on a 13.6% revenue decline, and CSG operating margin rose from 6.6% to 7.6% in the worst PC year on record. Under demand shock Dell cuts operating expense, holds price and accepts the revenue.
  • AI servers, Q3 FY2024 to Q1 FY2027: a step-change. AI-optimized server revenue went $1,873M, $9,286M, $24,683M, then $16,132M in one quarter. The step-change is Q4 FY2026, when backlog went from $18.4B to $43B on $34.1B of orders. AI servers were 2.1% of consolidated revenue in FY2024, 21.7% in FY2026 and 36.8% in Q1 FY2027. The balance sheet turned with it: core debt rose $4.0B in FY2026, the first material increase since FY2019; non-trade receivables from three contract manufacturers went $5.4B to $13.2B; accounts receivable went $10.3B to $17.6B. Dell will take low-margin revenue at scale when operating leverage covers it, and it will fund the working capital with the balance sheet it spent eight years repairing.

Patterns

Under demand shock, cut operating expense, hold price, keep the earnings. FY2020 and FY2023–FY2024 both show it. Consolidated operating expense went $15,658M to $15,013M to $14,558M across FY2024 to FY2026, down 7% while revenue grew 28%.

Under windfall, lean into volume and share and let the margin rate go. AI servers earn a mid-single-digit rate against ISG's blended 11.7%, and Q4 FY2026 CSG earned a 4.7% quarterly margin bought with a share push.

Change the capital structure instead of acquiring. Going private, EMC, Class V and the VMware spin were all structural, as were the divestitures of Dell Services, Dell Software, RSA, Boomi, Virtustream and Secureworks. Since EMC, Dell's answer to a strategic problem has consistently been a structure change.

Set targets high, miss them, then replace them without reconciling. The 12% consolidated operating margin for FY2023 was never reached and is never mentioned after the spin. The ISG 14% operating margin target for FY2023 was approached once, at 13.2%, and the segment has been below it in every year since, at 11.7% in FY2026. The company-level framework has been reset three times, in 2021, 2023 and 2025, with no bridge from the prior one.▪

Promote a strategic theme hard, then drop it silently. Mention counts across 39 earnings calls:

  • APEX: peaked at 10 mentions in Q1 FY2022 and is at zero in the FY2027 calls.
  • Recurring revenue: disclosed quarterly at $5–6B through Q3 FY2024 and not quantified since, though it remains a defined term in both Item 1 and Item 7 of the FY2026 10-K.
  • Edge and telecom: peaked at 14 mentions in Q2 FY2024 and is at five.
  • AI PC refresh: peaked at five and is at zero.

None was retired with an explanation.

10. Management, incentives and capital allocation

10.1 Who runs the company and what they are paid

Person Role Tenure FY2026 total pay
Michael S. Dell Chairman and CEO Founded Dell 1984 $3,382,209
Jeffrey W. Clarke COO and Vice Chairman Joined Dell 1987 $154,331,619
David Kennedy CFO (interim 2025-09-09, permanent 2025-11-24) At Dell since September 1998 $6,728,009
Richard J. Rothberg General Counsel — $10,196,585
William F. Scannell President, Global Sales and Customer Operations — $11,361,979
Yvonne McGill CFO to 2025-09-09; departed 2025-10-31 — $8,520,132 including $2,095,964 of severance-related pay

Michael Dell receives cash only: a $950,000 salary unchanged for at least a decade, with the proxy recording that the Committee honoured his request that it not consider an increase for FY2026, plus a cash bonus at 200% of salary. He has never received an equity grant as CEO. The FY2026 CEO pay ratio is 43 to 1.

The annual incentive plan pays on two metrics: non-GAAP net revenue at 50% and non-GAAP operating income at 50%. Performance share units add a three-year relative total shareholder return measure against the S&P 500 Information Technology Index at 50% of the grant. Absent from the annual plan are earnings per share, free cash flow, return on capital, margin and any capital-return metric. The company's public framework, set at the October 2025 analyst meeting, commits to 15%-plus non-GAAP diluted EPS growth, 100%-plus net income to adjusted free cash flow conversion, and returning 80%-plus of adjusted free cash flow.▪ None of those is a metric in the annual plan.

FY2026 outcomes: the business performance modifier came to 126% against a revenue plan of $102.3B and an operating income plan of $9.6B, with results of $111.8B and $10.2B. The footnote states that "For Fiscal 2026, there was no cap on the IBP business performance modifier, which was established to increase on a linear basis for performance above target." The FY2026 revenue plan was set 11.2% above FY2025 actual non-GAAP revenue and the operating income plan 12.9% above.

The FY2026 design feature. AI-optimized servers supplied $15,397M of the $17,971M consolidated revenue increase, or 85.7%. Had AI-server revenue been flat year over year, compensation revenue would have landed near $96.4B [estimate: disclosed compensation revenue of $111.8B less the disclosed $15,397M AI increment, assuming the excluded business operations contain no AI revenue, which the disclosure neither confirms nor denies], below the $102.3B plan and much nearer the $92.1B threshold. AI-optimized servers are the lowest-margin product Dell sells, the modifier is uncapped and linear above plan, and the operating-income half of the plan accounts for the other 50% while GAAP operating margin did improve across the period, from 6.1% in FY2024 to 7.2% in FY2026.

The Clarke option. Granted 2025-09-30, it is 2,500,000 Class C shares at a $141.77 exercise price with a ten-year term, cliff-vesting 2031-03-15 and forfeited in full if he retires or resigns first, with no acceleration on a change in control. Two goals must both be met, a market-capitalization goal and an adjusted free cash flow goal, and neither threshold is disclosed. Grant-date fair value was $132,400,000 on a Monte Carlo valuation, which is the entire gap between Clarke's $154.3M FY2026 total and his $21.9M of ordinary pay. The option was underwater at fiscal year-end when the Class C close was $114.44; at the 2026-08-12 close of $463.08 its intrinsic value is $803.3M, roughly 6x its grant-date fair value, ten months into a sixty-five-month vesting period. A market-capitalization goal is reduced dollar-for-dollar by a repurchase unless the stock re-rates, while the stated framework commits to returning 80%-plus of adjusted free cash flow, $7.5B of it in FY2026 alone.

Four figures are published for FY2026 operating income: $8,149M GAAP, $10.0B externally reported non-GAAP, $9.9B as the performance-share-unit result and $10.2B as the bonus-plan result. The proxy explains both gaps — the compensation measures exclude the results of certain business operations, and the bonus figure is struck before the bonus accrual itself — and neither convention is unusual. The effect is that no externally verifiable number is the number the bonus is paid on.

Dell has no stock ownership guidelines for directors or executive officers. Severance is 300% of base salary against twelve-month non-compete and non-solicit covenants. Equity is forfeited on termination including after a change in control, and the acceleration columns in the potential-payments table are blank. Hedging, pledging and margin accounts are prohibited for directors, officers, employees and their households.

The compensation committee has two members, and the proxy states that one of them "serves as a member of the Compensation Committee as the MD stockholders' nominee." Silver Lake waived its equivalent right.

10.2 Ownership and insider behaviour

As of the 2026-04-27 record date there were 276,744,341 Class A and 47,789,758 Class B shares at ten votes each against 325,034,188 Class C at one vote: 649,568,287 shares and 3,570,375,178 votes, so Class A and B together hold 90.9% of the voting power on 50.0% of the shares. Michael Dell personally held 246,834,081 Class A and 18,840,608 Class C at 2026-04-27, 40.9% of all outstanding stock and roughly $123 billion at $463.08.

His disposals are large and have stopped. Form 4 filings record 63,253,968 shares sold for roughly $7.85 billion between March 2024 and October 2025 at an average near $124, plus 25,539,014 shares gifted between October 2023 and October 2025. His beneficial holding went from 351,785,336 shares and 48.2% at the 2023 record date to 265,674,689 and 40.9% at 2026-04-27. Those 63.3 million shares would be worth about $29.3 billion at $463.08, against the roughly $7.85 billion realized. He has not sold a share since 2025-10-09, through a 305% advance from the $114.44 fiscal-year-end close to $463.08, and has never bought on the open market in this window.

Silver Lake is exiting. Class B holdings went from 136,986,858 shares and 19.1% of the company in the 2019 proxy to 47,789,758 and 7.4% at 2026-04-27, and to 44,351,394 by a 2026-06-15 8-K, a 68% reduction. Form 4s filed 2026-07-08 through 2026-07-14 record Silver Lake entity sales at an average near $440 per share. Silver Lake's board seat and committee-nomination rights persist under the stockholders agreement until it falls below 5% of the Class C-equivalent count, which on the present trajectory is close.

10.3 Governance: the Texas redomestication

The redomestication was approved at the 2026-06-25 annual meeting and took effect 2026-07-01.

Provision Delaware (before) Texas (after)
Derivative-suit standing no ownership threshold must beneficially own at least 3% of outstanding stock
Jury trial on internal entity claims not applicable in Chancery waived in the charter
Officer liability — may be limited or eliminated for monetary damages
Business judgment rule case law codified, with added protection for conflict-of-interest transactions
Books and records any stockholder with a proper purpose at least 5% holding, or at least six months of holding
Shareholder proposals SEC thresholds the board intends to adopt a bylaw electing a $1,000,000-or-3% threshold held six months, plus solicitation of holders of 67% of the voting power
Forum Delaware Texas exclusive forum

Three percent of 649,568,287 shares is 19,487,049 shares, about $9.0 billion at $463.08. On the 2026-04-27 ownership table, the holders above that threshold are Michael Dell, the Silver Lake stockholders, Vanguard at 22,512,097 shares and BlackRock at 22,819,963. The 67% solicitation requirement cannot be satisfied by any Class C holder, because Michael Dell and Silver Lake alone control 90.9% of the votes. The proxy's own stated motivation names the case that makes this material: in 2023 Dell paid $1 billion in cash to stockholders, including $266.7 million in attorneys' fees, in settlement of claims relating to the December 2018 Class V transaction, which was a controlling-stockholder conflict claim. The board also flagged the counterweight, noting that a meaningful body of case law interpreting the Texas amendments has not yet developed and that litigation challenging certain of them is pending. Dell is a controlled company entitled to skip the majority-independent-board and independent-committee requirements and complies with all three voluntarily, has a Lead Independent Director with agenda and information approval rights, and raised independent representation to 75% of the board.

At the 2026 annual meeting, both the say-on-pay proposal and the redomestication passed on 96.9% of total voting power. Class A and Class B cast 3,245,147,348 votes on the redomestication with zero against and zero abstentions, and subtracting that block from the combined total isolates a Class C result of 112,967,134 for against 107,690,029 withheld, or 51.2% support among the only traded class. The 8-K reports say-on-pay only on a combined basis with all series voting together, so a Class C say-on-pay figure cannot be derived directly from it; applying the same control-block totals implies support near 52%, against 92.1% for the equivalent 2025 vote computed the same way. Support for the Lead Independent Director on the Class C-only arithmetic was 52.6% against 56.7% a year earlier, and for the compensation committee chair, who stands on a Class C-only ballot, 88.8% against 97.6%. The FY2026 proxy, written before that vote, tells shareholders that FY2025 say-on-pay received approximately 99% support and adds that the Committee considers support received specifically from Class C stockholders, without publishing a Class C figure.

Q1 FY2026 retired 22.1 million shares, more than the 22.0 million retired in all of FY2025, at the lowest price of any quarter since FY2024. Inside the quarter Dell bought 3.1M shares at $108.93 in February 2025, 6.3M at $95.58 in March, then 12.7M at $82.48 between 2025-03-29 and 2025-05-02. Dell bought harder as the price declined. Against a benchmark of spending the same annual dollars at each fiscal year's volume-weighted price, FY2023–FY2026 would have acquired 171.4M shares and Dell acquired 172.0M, so timing added 0.35%. The economics came from persistence and scale: since the September 2021 programme began Dell has spent $15,856M to retire 194.6M shares at a blended $81.49.

The cumulative $18,335M reconciles exactly to management's "$18.3B cumulative return since dividend inception." The annual figures range from 56% to 251%, so the 80%-plus target is true only on a multi-year average and the window chosen moves the answer. Management quoted 97% at the October 2025 meeting, correct through the first half of FY2026, and the second-half cash surge dropped the four-year cumulative to 84.3%. And on GAAP free cash flow Dell has returned 108.5% of the cash it generated over four years, funded by $3,843M of cumulative DFS financing-receivable add-backs plus the FY2026 debt raise. The add-back is defensible in principle because DFS receivables are funded with matched, largely non-recourse DFS debt, and it means the denominator management measures itself against is systematically larger than the cash left after the business's own working-capital needs, with the gap widening exactly when DFS is growing fastest.

Per-share outcomes. Diluted weighted-average shares declined 13.5% from the FY2022 peak of 791M to 684M in FY2026; shares outstanding declined 13.9%, from 757M to 652M, and to 649M at 2026-05-01. Revenue per diluted share compounded at 6.7% a year over FY2022–FY2026 against absolute revenue at 2.9%, and operating income per diluted share at 19.3% against 15.0%. The share count contributed 3.6 points of that 19.3%, about 19% of it; the rest is margin and mix. Gross equity-award issuance has declined from 3.2% of the share base to 1.4%, and stock-based compensation from $1,622M to $723M, so buybacks have been accretive.

The dividend. It was initiated at $0.33 a quarter in Q1 FY2023 and raised 12%, 20%, 18% and 20% since, to $0.630 a quarter for FY2027, compounding at 17.5% a year against a stated commitment of 10% or more, first set through FY2028 and extended through FY2030.▪ Management confirmed the commitment is per share, so buybacks do not reduce it. The dividend consumed 62.9% of adjusted free cash flow in FY2023 and 12.7% in FY2026.

Capital expenditure. It has run at roughly 1.0x the depreciation of tangible and capitalized-software assets for three straight years, and at 1.5%–3.1% of revenue across the decade. Dell does not disclose a maintenance-versus-growth split and on this arithmetic there is not much of a growth component to disclose. Growth capital goes into working capital and DFS: in FY2026 inventories rose $3,987M, receivables $7,022M and financing receivables $2,740M, $13,749M of gross investment, against a $12,665M increase in payables.

The inflection in the buyback arithmetic. At a $148 average purchase price the Q1 FY2027 buyback retired half as many shares as Q1 FY2026 for 82% of the money, and guidance for Q2 FY2027 is roughly 652M diluted shares against 656M in Q1. With the stock at $464.05, the same dollar now retires roughly one-fifth of the shares it retired in Q1 FY2026. The framework is denominated in a percentage of cash flow, so reported capital return can keep growing while the share-count contribution to EPS growth goes toward zero. Adjusted free cash flow of $3,165M in Q1 FY2027 against $2,092M returned is 66%, below the 80% target, with cash still building.

Management has never stated a return or internal-rate hurdle for M&A or capital expenditure.

11. M&A, divestitures and deal track record

Dell is not a serial acquirer and has not been one for a decade. One transaction dominates: $58,703M of consideration transferred for EMC on 2016-09-07, followed by ten years of selling, deleveraging and, since the VMware spin, near-total abstention from buying. The operating businesses Dell bought have performed poorly: EMC's crown jewel was storage, and Dell's storage net revenue was $15,254M in FY2018, its first full year owning EMC, and $16,631M in FY2026, a 1.09% compound annual rate over eight years, below US inflation over the same window. Excluding AI-optimized servers from FY2026 ISG, the segment grew from $30,652M to $36,143M over the same eight years, a 2.08% rate. The AI-driven profit growth came from the server line Dell already owned before EMC. Dell has never taken one dollar of goodwill impairment on the $31,539M of EMC goodwill, of which $15,315M remains in ISG. It has been willing to impair elsewhere: it wrote off $397M of goodwill and $809M of gross assets against Virtustream, roughly two-thirds of a $1,220M purchase price.

The financial transactions went the other way. Dell repaid roughly $7.0B of EMC merger debt within five months of closing by selling three businesses and reached investment grade at all three agencies. It extracted $18,170M of VMware special dividends in two tranches and distributed a VMware stake to its own shareholders that Broadcom valued at roughly $61B two years later. It sold Boomi for $4.0B at roughly 20x revenue while its own equity traded near 0.5x revenue.

The capital-structure transaction. The Class V buy-in was announced 2018-07-02 at a theoretical ~$109 per share with a $9B cash cap and enhanced on 2018-11-14 to $120 with the cap raised to $14B. The enhancement followed Carl Icahn's public opposition to the first offer and binding voting agreements signed with Elliott Management and others holding roughly 17% of the Class V stock. It added roughly $2.2B of implied value, and Dell changed the terms under shareholder pressure.

Synergy tracking stopped. The stated targets were $2.0B of merger cost synergies within about eighteen months plus $1.0B of standalone cost actions, and roughly $700M of annual VMware revenue synergies. Management never reported a realized figure against the cost targets. The closest thing to a progress report is the CFO's Q3 FY2017 answer: "I'm not going to parse it for you, I would tell you that we're generally on track." Counting mentions of the word across 39 earnings calls and 60 presentations, there are 10 in Q3 FY2017, 6 in Q4 FY2017, 6 in Q4 FY2020 and 19 across the September 2018 analyst day, then effectively nothing, and zero quantified updates after FY2020.

Definite-lived intangibles from the deal are nearly spent. Gross $27,044M against accumulated amortization of $25,566M leaves $1,478M net plus $3,055M of indefinite-lived trade names. Amortization of intangibles in the segment reconciliation declined from $833M in FY2024 to $667M and then $497M. The non-cash earnings drag from the deal is 94.5% finished, while the goodwill remains unimpaired.

What the EMC deal left behind. Dell was taken private in October 2013 at roughly $24.9B of equity on $56.9B of revenue, about 0.4x sales, and three years later bought EMC at roughly 2.2x sales. Dell had no public equity multiple at the time because it was private, so there was no market check. What the operating company retained is a storage business that has not grown in nominal dollars since FY2018 plus $19,547M of unimpaired goodwill. The value that was realized came almost entirely from the VMware leg, and the cash from it went to retiring EMC debt while the equity went to shareholders directly.

Post-spin acquisition spending. Cash spent on acquisitions from FY2022 through Q1 FY2027 totals $296M against roughly $40B of operating cash flow, a 142x step down from the $42,145M of FY2017–FY2021. Management has repeated the same language at every analyst meeting since 2021 — tuck-in and IP-accretive, nothing significant, no large-scale transformational transactions — and the spending matches it exactly.

12. Capitalization and balance sheet

Dell is an investment-grade issuer with roughly $16.7B of corporate debt against $11.6B of cash, a fully undrawn $6.0B revolver, an unused $5.0B commercial paper programme and no meaningful near-term corporate maturity. The largest claims on this balance sheet are $45.3B of accounts payable and $20.8B of purchase obligations.

Legacy Notes are $952M of unsecured pre-2013 Dell Inc. paper at 7.10% due 2028 ($300M), 6.50% due 2038 ($388M) and 5.40% due 2040 ($264M).

Weighted-average cost of debt. Principal-weighted coupon across the corporate stack: Senior Notes 5.21% on $21,800M, Legacy Notes 6.38% on $952M, combined 5.26% on $22,752M at 2026-01-30 and 5.24% on $22,252M after the Q1 FY2027 repayment of the 6.02% June 2026 notes. All of it is fixed-rate, so the coupon is also the cash rate. FY2026 interest expense of $1,560M on average total debt of $28,035M implies a 5.56% blended all-in rate across corporate plus DFS debt; applying 5.26% to $22.8B of corporate paper leaves roughly $361M against roughly $8.9B of average DFS debt, about 4.1%, consistent with the disclosed DFS rate structure.

Refinancing cost at current rates is close to zero. Dell's two most recent issuances priced at 4.75%–5.50% in April 2025 and 4.15%–5.10% in October 2025, at or below the embedded average. The exception is the €500M Dell Bank 0.5% eurobond maturing October 2026, which refinances into a euro market where Dell's most recent Dell Bank issue priced at 3.60%, roughly a 310 basis-point step-up on about $580M, or $18M of incremental annual interest.

The maturity wall is mostly DFS. Of the $31.8B of principal at 2026-01-30, $22.6B is corporate and other debt with $2.3B payable within twelve months, against $9.1B of DFS debt with $5.7B payable within twelve months. The corporate wall in FY2027 is the $0.5B June 2026 notes, since repaid, plus the $1.75B October 2026 notes; after that the corporate stack amortizes at roughly $1.0–2.5B a year through FY2031 with $12.5B thereafter, against $10.6B of trailing operating income.

Floating and FX exposure are immaterial. Borrowings exposed to interest-rate fluctuations were $3.0 billion of $31.5 billion at 2026-01-30, all inside DFS, and a 100 basis-point increase would raise annual interest expense by approximately $30 million. Interest-rate contract notionals were $7,048M, used to swap DFS floating exposure to fixed to match fixed-rate customer leases. FX hedge notionals were $13,378M with a disclosed one-day 95% value at risk of $6 million.

Leases and pension are rounding errors. The operating lease liability was $727M at 2026-01-30 with a 4.11-year weighted term at a 4.74% discount rate, 2.3% of total debt; there are no material finance leases. The US pension plan assumed from EMC and frozen since December 1999 was terminated and fully settled on 2025-09-24 with a $15M net gain. International defined-benefit plans are $248M underfunded and there is no disclosed post-retirement benefit obligation.

Covenants. The revolver is subject to one interest-coverage covenant tested quarterly, with which Dell was in compliance at 2026-01-30; the level is not disclosed, so headroom cannot be computed. There is no maintenance covenant in the indentures and no leverage covenant anywhere. The FY2026 10-K risk factor states that the existing debt terms "generally do not restrict our ability to incur additional unsecured debt" and contain significant exceptions to the secured-debt covenant. The covenant risk is in DFS. The US asset-based financing facility and the European securitization facility each contain structural features tied to the performance of the funded receivables: defined credit losses, delinquencies, average credit scores and minimum collection requirements. If those are not met and the facility cannot be restructured, no further funding of receivables is permitted. Both were in compliance at 2026-01-30, on a receivables book whose growth is now attributed primarily to AI-optimized servers.

Core debt is a figure management defines itself. At 2026-01-30, Senior Notes of $21,573M plus Legacy Notes of $952M less "DFS allocated debt" of $5,507M gives core debt of $17,018M. That $5,507M is Dell's own Senior Notes, moved out of core debt and into the DFS allocation by applying a management-chosen 7:1 debt-to-equity ratio to $16,739M of DFS owned assets. The allocation grew from $1,640M in FY2024 to $3,028M in FY2025 to $5,507M in FY2026 as the DFS book grew, so $3.9B of Senior Notes moved out of core debt over two years without a dollar being repaid.

The deleveraging arc. Total debt principal peaked at $54,239M at 2019-02-01 and core debt at $41,166M at 2017-02-03. Management's own core leverage ratio, quoted on earnings calls, went 4.2x at the FY2019 opening, 3.2x at FY2020, roughly 2.5x at FY2021 and 1.9x at Q3 FY2022. It was 1.5x at Q4 FY2024 and 1.2x at Q4 FY2025, back to 1.6x in Q1 FY2026 on the debt issuance, and 1.2x at Q1 FY2027. Fitch upgraded the long-term issuer default rating and senior unsecured rating to BBB+ from BBB with a stable outlook on 2025-09-30, citing sustained core EBITDA leverage below 2x since fiscal 2024 and rapid growth in the AI server business, with a downgrade sensitivity above 2.0x and a further-upgrade sensitivity below 1.5x [web]. An S&P rating action titled as an upgrade to BBB+ was published around June 2026 [web, unverified].

Stock-based compensation is 0.64% of FY2026 revenue and 0.43% of Q1 FY2027 revenue, and it has declined in absolute dollars every year since FY2022. The forward pipeline is small and shrinking: restricted share units outstanding went from 50M at 2023-02-03 to 19M at 2026-01-30, grants from 23M units in FY2024 to 8M in FY2026, and unrecognized stock-based compensation is $0.7B over a 1.7-year weighted period. Class A and Class B conversions inflate the issued share count without diluting anyone — 10M of Class C issued on conversion in FY2026, 100M in FY2025 — so issued shares rose from 834M to 852M while outstanding declined from 696M to 649M.

Structural risks

  1. The funding of the AI ramp is trade payables. Accounts payable rose $11,661M in one quarter while total debt declined $350M. Supplier terms are negotiated, and in a component squeeze where suppliers hold allocation power they can shorten terms or demand prepayment. The leading indicators are the cash conversion cycle and the supply-chain finance balance inside payables, which rose 55% to $3.1B in one quarter.
  2. Purchase obligations have gone from a footnote to a balance-sheet-scale commitment, from $5.0B at FY2024 to $20.8B at 2026-05-01, and the disclosed number now excludes fixed-quantity strategic-supplier commitments priced after the balance-sheet date. $16.9B falls in the remaining nine months of FY2027 against $15.1B of inventory already on the books.
  3. Customer credit is migrating onto the balance sheet through two channels at once, trade receivables at $25,854M with a 0.30% allowance rate, and DFS financing receivables at $14.3B written to a mix that got 9.6 percentage points worse in a year.
  4. DFS facility renewals inside twelve months. $5,719M of DFS debt was short-term at 2026-01-30, 63% of the book, and it rolls on the performance of receivables whose character has just changed.
  5. The revolver matures 2027-11-01, undrawn but the backstop for the $5.0B commercial paper programme.
  6. Structural subordination. The obligor group generated $7,769M of FY2026 revenue against $113,538M consolidated and holds $20,200M of total assets against $101,286M, so a recovery analysis cannot start from consolidated assets. The guarantee package covers the parent chain and the notes are investment grade.
  7. Covenant-light incurrence. With $15.2B of buyback authorization remaining and a rating-agency threshold of 2.0x core EBITDA leverage against a current 1.2x, incremental debt capacity before a downgrade trigger is roughly $11B at the current EBITDA run rate [estimate: 2.0x roughly $13.9B of adjusted EBITDA less $16.7B of core debt]. Only management's stated policy constrains it.
  8. Negative book equity is an artifact. At 2026-05-01, common stock and capital in excess of par were $9,111M against treasury stock at cost of $(16,149)M, retained earnings of +$6,343M and accumulated other comprehensive loss of $(709)M. Retained earnings crossed from a $(1,160)M deficit at 2025-01-31 to +$6,343M, so at the Q1 FY2027 pace book equity turns positive within roughly one to two quarters absent a buyback step-up.

Dell Financial Services. DFS's financing revenue, its net spread over securitization cost and its return on the $14.3B receivable book plus $2.5B of equipment under operating leases are not quantified, and neither is the residual value the 10-K discusses four times. That matters because DFS is used explicitly to pull AI demand forward, and because any residual assumption depends on a secondary market for three-year-old GPU servers.

13.3 What drove the record

Growth. Consolidated revenue compounded at 6.9% over nine years and 5.5% over five, a blend of ISG at 13.0% and CSG at 1.1%, with Corporate and other shrinking from $5,382M to $1,728M and acting as a mechanical drag of roughly 70 basis points a year on consolidated growth. Acquisitions have added little to growth since FY2017: cash paid for acquisitions net of cash acquired was $37,629M for EMC and then $658M, $971M, $2,463M, $424M, $16M, $70M, $126M, nil and $84M. FY2026 revenue growth of 18.8% is entirely organic and is understated by roughly 190 basis points by the Corporate-and-other runoff.

Gross margin. Mix drives the gross-margin path, and it shows in incremental margins. Over FY2025 to FY2026, Dell added $17,971M of revenue and $1,457M of gross profit, an 8.1% incremental gross margin against a 22.2% starting-year average; over FY2024 to FY2025 the incremental rate was 2.5%. FY2022 declined 160 basis points on component cost inflation and logistics, with CSG revenue up 27% on lower-margin units. FY2024 rose 160 basis points as both segments' volumes declined sharply and mix moved toward storage and services, including a $200M revision benefit worth 23 basis points. FY2025 declined 160 basis points as AI-optimized servers scaled from $1,873M to $9,286M, and FY2026 declined 220 basis points as they reached $24,683M, 21.7% of revenue.

Operating margin. Incremental operating margin has run above incremental gross margin in both of the last two years, 11.6% against 2.5% in FY2025 and 10.6% against 8.1% in FY2026. Operating expenses declined from $18,273M in FY2020 to $14,558M in FY2026, and in every year since FY2022, a $3,715M reduction while revenue grew $28,723M, taking operating expense from 21.5% of revenue to 12.8%.▪ SG&A alone declined from $15,819M to $11,416M, so the entire reduction came out of SG&A while R&D rose from $2,454M to $3,142M. Operating margin expanded from 2.8% to 7.2% over FY2020–FY2026 while gross margin contracted from 24.3% to 20.0%.

Below the line. Interest and other, net moved from $(2,417)M in FY2020 to $(886)M in FY2026 as core debt declined from $33.8B to $13.0B before rising back to $17.0B. That $1,531M improvement is roughly the size of one year's operating-income growth and is not repeatable. The effective tax rate has ranged from 4.3% to 24.9% over FY2021–FY2026 with no discernible trend.

Returns. ROIC quadrupled over five years, from 8.5% to 36.0%, and two-thirds of that came from the denominator: NOPAT grew 89% while average invested capital declined 55%. Invested capital declined because EMC purchase-accounting intangibles amortized away, from $35,053M at FY2017 to $4,533M at FY2026, because the VMware spin removed roughly $30B of assets and associated debt, and because payables grew faster than receivables and inventory.

Working capital. In FY2026 days sales outstanding moved from 39 to 57, days inventory from 33 to 42, days payable from 102 to 135 and the cash conversion cycle from −30 to −37 days. The gross movements in the cash flow statement show receivables consuming $7,022M, financing receivables $2,740M and inventories $3,987M against payables releasing $12,665M, a net working-capital source of only $871M on $18.0B of incremental revenue. Days-payable on the reported line understates Dell's true payment terms because reported accounts payable is net of a $13.0B offset against non-trade receivables that grew 2.8x in one year.

Metrics that were discontinued. Recurring revenue was last quantified at $5.6B, up 4%, on the Q3 FY2024 call. It remains a defined term in Item 1 and Item 7 of the FY2026 10-K, unquantified for ten consecutive quarters. APEX annual recurring revenue was last quantified at over $1 billion in Q2 FY2023 and has not been quantified since. Both were retired at the point the unaudited AI backlog became the headline number.

Inflections in the current quarter. Revenue growth broke trend twice in two quarters, from 5%–19% year over year through Q3 FY2026 to 39.5% and then 87.5%. Mix moved about 15 points in one quarter, with AI-optimized servers at 21.7% of FY2026 revenue and 36.8% of Q1 FY2027, or 29.1% on a trailing-twelve-month basis. Gross margin and operating margin moved in opposite directions in the same filing, with GAAP gross margin down 330 basis points to 17.8% and GAAP operating margin up 330 basis points to 8.3%, bridged by SG&A plus R&D declining from 16.1% of revenue to 9.4% on a GAAP basis. CSG posted an 8.0% operating margin against 5.6% for FY2026, which management guided back to roughly 6% for Q2 FY2027 and explicitly said was not a run rate. Two series show continuity: storage has stayed in a $3.8–4.8B quarterly band for all twelve quarters and at the same annual level as FY2019, and CSG Consumer declined 47% from FY2021 to FY2026 before its first meaningful growth quarter in three years off a $1,463M base.

14. Expectations: internal, external and base rates

The headline disagreement is between the company and the street. Dell's own long-term framework implies FY2030 revenue of $148,825–160,268M; Bloomberg consensus is $235,734M, 47% higher, and management declined to revise the framework when asked directly on 2026-05-28.▪

Driver Internal (management) External (street) Where and why they disagree Base-rate
FY2027 revenue $165,000–169,000M guide, described as "only gated by supply" $170,982M mean, $169,000M median The median estimate matches the top of the guide and the mean is 1.2% above it The ten instances of +45% growth from a base above $100B in 33 years are all banks, oil majors, refiners or Berkshire, with no non-financial, non-commodity case among them
FY2027 non-GAAP EPS $17.90 ± $0.25 $18.35 mean, $18.17 median The median is two cents above the top of the guided range Dell has beaten initial annual EPS guidance every year since FY2020, mean +17.3%; the FY2027 guide has already been raised once so the beat base rate applies with less force
Q2 FY2027 revenue $44,000–45,000M $44,877M mean, standard deviation $410M (0.9%) No disagreement. The lowest published estimate is above the bottom of the guide —
FY2028–FY2030 revenue 7%–9% a year framework, never revised 11.3% a year Consensus is 47% above the top of the framework at FY2030 Post-boom class median 5.4%–6.3% a year, p75 11.5%–11.7%; consensus is at roughly the 74th percentile
FY2028 AI-server revenue not guided beyond FY2027 ~$65B to ~$117B implied, mean ~$86B [estimate: residual build] This $52B spread on one product line is more than twice Dell's FY2026 AI revenue and is where almost all the FY2028 dispersion originates Hardware boom years persist better than the all-sector base rate at a 20.1% median forward three-year rate, but almost every observation starts from a base below $20B

Every company in the comparison set saw gross margin decline as low-margin mix rose

The falling ratio is a denominator effect
Operating margin +>55% growth in FY2027; ISG 10%–14% band, CSG 5%–7% 9.4% FY2027E rising to 9.5% FY2029E and 10.3% FY2030E Both require operating-expense leverage to more than offset gross-margin dilution Of 39 company-years combining a 12%–22% gross margin with a 9%-plus operating margin above $20B of revenue, all 39 belong to Chevron, Exxon, Marathon, Boeing, Berkshire or Tesla. None is a technology company

Cash flow 100%+ net income to adjusted FCF conversion; 80%+ of adjusted FCF returned every Bloomberg cash-flow consensus field returns empty The street's expectation for Dell is a profit-and-loss statement and nothing else, while the risk in a supply-constrained, inventory-forward ramp is cash conversion —
ROIC not published as a target not published — 24.7% start; the reference class fades top-quartile returns by a median 6.1 to 7.3 percentage points over three to five years

Management's guidance record. Across eighteen consecutive quarters from Q4 FY2022, revenue beat the midpoint 13 times at a median +2.3%, and non-GAAP EPS beat 16 times at a median +10.8%. The conservatism is below the revenue line, in cost, pricing discipline and operating expense, and the EPS beat has run roughly 4–5x the revenue beat. Guidance precision degrades exactly when the environment moves, and it degrades to the upside: FY2024 quarterly EPS beats ran +29% to +64% in the demand trough, compressed to +3% to +15% in the stable years, and reached +67.6% in Q1 FY2027. The two EPS misses share a shape: revenue in line or better, profitability short.

The annual revenue guide has less forecasting value across a cycle turn. It has been wrong by −4.7% in FY2023, −2.1% in FY2020 and +10.2% in FY2026, and is already tracking +19.3% for FY2027 after one quarter. FY2025 is the one case of serial raises followed by a shortfall: Dell raised the revenue guide twice to a $97,000M midpoint and finished at $95,600M, below even the reduced third-quarter view, because the PC refresh did not arrive on schedule. Dell is again mid-way through a serial raise driven by one product category.

The arithmetic problem inside the framework. On management's own stated baseline — FY2026 guidance of $107,000M revenue and $9.55 EPS as of 2025-08-28, running through FY2030 — the targets are $151,000M of revenue at the 9% top end and $16.70 of EPS at 15%. The FY2027 guidance issued seven months later, $167,000M and $17.90, exceeds both. Using the FY2026 actuals instead gives $160,200M and $18.01, and the FY2027 revenue guide still exceeds the revenue target. Either the framework is re-based at the next analyst meeting, or Dell's own FY2027 guidance implies flat-to-declining revenue from FY2028 through FY2030.▪

The guide against seasonality. Consensus puts 48.2% of FY2027 revenue in the second half and Dell's guide puts 47.1%, against an eight-year Dell average of 51.3%. A normal Dell second half applied to a fixed first half of $88,342M implies FY2027 revenue of $181,400M [estimate: first half divided by one minus 51.3%], $10.4B above the consensus mean. The street has moved about $4B of the way from the guide toward normal seasonality and stopped, while holding a full-year mean above the top of the guide. Those two positions are hard to hold together: if the supply constraint justifies a 48% second half, the full year should be at or below the guide.

A distortion in the published dispersion. The FY2027 EPS low of $13.04 is 29% below the mean and 26% below the bottom of Dell's own guided range, 3.9 standard deviations from the mean on 26 contributors, and is almost exactly the consensus mean as of 2026-04-30, the last month before the Q1 print. The FY2027 revenue low of $167,122M is inside the guided range and is clearly current. Excluding the stale EPS low, FY2027 dispersion is $17.00–$19.71 on plus or minus one standard deviation, a 15% spread against the published 42%.

The memory-cost episode. On 2025-11-18 Morgan Stanley downgraded Dell two notches to underweight and cut its FY2027 gross-margin forecast by 220 basis points to 18.2%, citing NAND and DRAM spot prices up 50% to 300% in six months and OEM ability to offset only about 70% of memory inflation [web]. Consensus FY2027 gross margin today is 17.76%, slightly below that bear case, so the margin call was right and slightly too optimistic. Consensus FY2027 EPS is $18.35, roughly 82% above where that note left its own estimate. Volume and operating leverage outweighed the mix effect. In this cycle, gross-margin-rate forecasts have not predicted the direction of Dell's earnings.

Ratings drift the other way from estimates. Buy ratings peaked at 24 in October 2025 with the stock at $162 and stand at 21 with the stock at $464; holds doubled from five to ten; the average rating declined from 4.66 to 4.32 across a period in which FY2027 consensus EPS rose 59%. On 2026-04-30 the consensus target was 8.1% below the market price. The published target series follows price with a lag.

15. Market pricing and valuation history

Descriptive record only. This section contains no valuation judgment: no cheap or expensive conclusion, no fair value, no price target, no view on the stock.

The price history covers 7.6 years, because Class C began regular-way trading on 2018-12-28 through the Class V transaction; the predecessor tracking stock tracked Dell's economic interest in VMware and is not chained here. Bloomberg back-adjusts every pre-2021-11-02 price by about 0.506x for the VMware distribution, so price levels, market capitalization and every multiple here use the as-traded series while returns use the spin-adjusted series. Bloomberg's own forward-P/E field divides the spin-adjusted price by consensus EPS, so it prints roughly half the multiple the stock traded at before November 2021; the series used here is recomputed as the as-traded close divided by consensus EPS.

Perfect-foresight forward P/E divides the fiscal-year-end price by the next year's actual adjusted EPS, so it uses hindsight. FY2019 through FY2022 multiples are on a Dell-including-VMware basis and are internally consistent but not comparable to FY2023 onward. Enterprise value uses GAAP total debt including Dell Financial Services borrowings; recomputing FY2026 on core debt alone gives $80,105M and EV/EBITDA of 7.0x against 8.3x. Neither treatment is complete, because excluding DFS debt without also excluding the DFS receivables and earnings it funds is asymmetric.

Price-to-book is omitted. Dell's total common equity has been negative in seven of the last eight fiscal years and Bloomberg returns a null price-to-book today, publishing the field for only 403 of 1,918 sessions.

The −60% drawdown from May 2024 to April 2025 opened the session after the Q1 FY2025 print, on a guide-down in gross-margin rate, and ended at the April 2025 tariff low. Over that window twelve-month-forward consensus EPS rose from $8.21 to $9.47, about 15%, while the forward multiple compressed from 17.0x to 9.7x. On month-end sampling the price declined 34% and the multiple change accounts for 134% of the log move, with rising estimates working against it. The market was marking down what it would pay for AI-server earnings, and the trigger was the disclosed margin structure of that revenue. The −58.6% drawdown into March 2020 is COVID. The −44.4% drawdown through October 2022 spans the post-pandemic PC unwind and the FY2024 revenue decline, and its trough coincided with the lowest forward multiple since listing, 4.9x.

The largest rally since listing is the current one: +305.5% from the FY2026 close of $114.44 on 2026-01-30 to $464.05 on 2026-08-12, of which one session supplied +32.8% and another +21.9%, with a −20.7% drawdown inside it that recovered in 64 days.

17. Forward model summary

Operating model only. No valuation, no multiples applied to these projections, no discounting, no view on the stock.

A gap that qualifies everything in this section. Management names memory supply as the constraint on FY2027 revenue — the guide is "only gated by supply" and "demand far exceeds available supply" — and none of the model's 29 drivers is a component-availability variable. Both scenarios stress demand in a year management says is set by procurement; neither tests Dell winning orders it cannot source.

17.1 What the model produces

FY2026 actual FY2027 FY2028 FY2029 FY2030 FY2031 FY2032 CAGR
Revenue, bear 113,538 157,431 146,010 127,272 119,252 115,951 115,665 +0.3%
Revenue, base 113,538 167,411 182,537 184,248 180,389 177,464 179,982 +8.0%
Revenue, bull 113,538 178,389 222,530 247,070 265,435 280,955 295,801 +17.3%
Non-GAAP EPS, bear 10.30 14.00 9.74 6.59 6.13 6.55 6.95 (6.3)%
Non-GAAP EPS, base 10.30 17.75 20.06 20.37 20.60 21.41 22.91 +14.3%
Non-GAAP EPS, bull 10.30 21.15 30.47 37.67 44.34 50.66 57.35 +33.1%
Free cash flow, base 8,552 8,845 10,332 11,119 11,450 11,622 11,758

Revenue peaks and then declines in the base case, and that is a price effect. Base-case revenue peaks at $184,248M in FY2029 and declines through FY2031. Underneath it, traditional-server units grow every year and PC units grow after FY2027. The decline is the reversal of memory-driven average-selling-price inflation: base-case traditional-server ASP gives back roughly half of its FY2027 gain over FY2029–FY2030, and CSG revenue per unit gives back most of its FY2027 gain over FY2028–FY2029.▪ Consensus has revenue rising in every year to FY2031 and therefore contains no normalization year at all.

Operating income is far more stable than revenue, because the revenue that deflates never had much margin in it. Base-case non-GAAP operating income is $15,585M in FY2027 and $16,545M in FY2032, a 1.0% annual change across a period in which revenue swings from $167B to $184B and back to $180B. Pass-through revenue enters at close to cost, so when it leaves it takes little profit with it.▪

The AI-server line moves the model least. A ±35% move in AI-server volume from FY2028, calibrated to the published dispersion of the FY2028 street estimate, changes FY2032 operating income by ±$1,251M and six-year cumulative free cash flow by ±$1,107M. A 250 basis-point move in ISG core gross margin changes cumulative free cash flow by ±$6,440M.

17.2 How the model is built

Revenue is built from the units-and-price decomposition each business has. AI-optimized servers are modelled through the disclosed backlog roll-forward — opening backlog plus orders booked less closing backlog — because Dell discloses no AI unit counts and no system prices, and external rack-price estimates span $3.0M to $6.5M. Traditional servers are units times average selling price. Storage is Dell-IP growth plus third-party resale runoff ending at end-FY2027. CSG is Dell PC units times revenue per unit. Consolidated operating income is the two segments plus Corporate and other, less intangible amortization, stock-based compensation and other corporate expenses.

Scenario FY2027 FY2028 FY2029 FY2030 FY2031 FY2032
base orders booked 78,000 72,000 68,000 62,000 58,000 62,000
closing backlog 61,000 59,000 49,000 39,000 31,000 28,000
AI revenue 60,000 74,000 78,000 72,000 66,000 65,000
bear AI revenue 55,000 55,000 45,000 38,000 34,000 33,000
bull AI revenue 66,000 98,000 115,000 125,000 132,000 138,000

FY2026 actual orders were $64,100M, shipments $25,200M and closing backlog $43,000M.

17.3 Assumptions and where each is contested

Driver Base Bear Bull Counter-argument
AI-optimized server orders booked, FY2027 $78,000M — — The driver is not independently identified: revenue is opening backlog plus orders less closing backlog, so only the difference between this and the closing-backlog driver is constrained, and FY2027 solves to the guide midpoint by construction. Dell guides AI-server revenue, never orders
AI-optimized server orders booked, FY2028 $72,000M $45,000M $105,000M The base's AI revenue output is systematically 14%–16% below the street's residual range at every point, with the bear 15% below the lowest published street estimate. The cited evidence does not support the range set, though an independent discount to the street is defensible on the post-boom base rate
AI-optimized server orders booked, FY2030 $62,000M $30,000M $135,000M Applying the mechanism-matched refiner fade of −8.0% a year to the FY2027 base gives $60,700M against the $62,000M base, and the 4.5x range brackets both mechanisms
AI closing backlog, FY2028 $59,000M $46,000M — The series is five quarters old, appears in no filing, uses an unpublished definition and has no disclosed cancellation terms. No scenario contains a backlog cancellation, and the FY2028 bear of $46,000M is still 7% above the FY2026 exit level
AI-optimized server gross margin 5.3% rising to 5.5% 4.0% declining to 3.5% 6.5% rising to 7.5% The Q1 FY2027 reconstruction implies 2.9%–4.5% depending on the core rate, so the latest quarter is at or below the bear. The base improves the rate from FY2029 when management calls mid-single digits non-negotiable. At ±150bp this is ±$975M of FY2032 operating income
Traditional server unit growth, FY2028 +5% (6)% — The base grows units in all six years in a line whose units declined in FY2025 and FY2026 on the 10-K's own attribution and turned positive only in the two quarters management conceded buy-ahead. The bear allows two down years and returns to growth by FY2030, milder than the −19.5% Dell units printed in its own last pull-forward payback
Traditional server ASP growth, FY2027 +49% — — This is a residual: base units +8% times ASP +49% reproduces the guided "just over 60%" by construction, and management explicitly refused the split ("I won't parse out the specifics"). This driver ranks first of seven on terminal operating income at −$2,400M/+$2,806M
Traditional server ASP growth, FY2029 (12)% (22)% 0% The base holds ASP up 2% in FY2028 and starts the give-back a year later than its own cited normalization schedule, and the index still compounds to 1.271 by FY2030, so Dell permanently retains 27 points of memory-driven price after peaking at +52%
Storage revenue growth, FY2028 +9% — +14% Storage grew in every year of every scenario, and the bear reaches $19,284M by FY2032, above the top of a seven-year band in which the line compounded at −0.1% and printed a −9.5% year. The FY2028 step-up itself is mechanical and dated: the crossover ends
ISG core gross margin 38.2% 35.5% declining to 34.5% 40.0% rising to 41.0% The FY2024 solve is an independent anchor and the model holds core 190bp below it throughout. It is the largest cumulative-cash driver in the model at ±$6,440M and depends on a Dell-IP versus third-party split Dell has never published
ISG operating expense growth +6% +2% then (3)% and (2)% +5% The range is degenerate where it matters: no scenario has ISG operating expense growing faster than 6% a year after FY2027, and this driver ranks second of seven on terminal operating income. Q1 FY2027 consolidated R&D grew 22% and SG&A 6% on variable compensation
Dell PC unit growth, FY2027 (5)% — (2)% The justification cites Dell units −5.0% in Q2 CY2026 as support for outgrowing the market by six points, but in that quarter the market was −4.9% and Dell's share was flat. Over three years Dell's unit share declined 230bp, and in CY2025 Dell undergrew the market in the year the refresh peaked
Dell PC unit growth, FY2028 +2% (2)% +5% Dell's own precedent for a PC pull-forward produced industry units −14.8% and Dell units −19.5%; the bear here is −2%, seventeen points milder. IDC forecasts CY2026 units −11.3% with declines reaching 20% by the fourth quarter
CSG revenue per unit, FY2027 +19% — — A residual of the CSG revenue guide divided by the unit assumption; the published band is an artifact of fixing units at −5%. Realized revenue per unit moved +4.4%, +0.9% and +0.4% across FY2024–FY2026 and +8.6% in Q1 FY2027, less than half the assumed full-year rate
CSG revenue per unit, FY2028 (6)% (10)% 0% IDC expects no PC memory relief until early 2028, so a −6% price year in FY2028 assumes deflation begins roughly twelve months before the cited schedule. The treatment is also asymmetric: on the way up a third of each increase goes unrecovered, on the way down cost is assumed to fall almost exactly in step
CSG gross margin 14.4% 12.7% — CSG gross margin is now the segment's only scenario driver because operating expense is pinned across bear and base, and the base holds 14.2%–15.0% through two years in which revenue per unit falls 6% then 4%. Q4 FY2026 printed 14.16% and Q1 FY2027 16.46%, a 230bp swing between consecutive quarters
CSG operating expense, % of revenue 8.8% 8.8% 8.8% Bear equals base, so the driver has no downside case. Holding a rate constant through a revenue decline is the aggressive assumption, and the fixed half of the block is growing: CSG R&D intensity rose every year to 1.31% in Q1 FY2027 with dollars up 41% year over year
Corporate and other revenue $600M — — Modelled at zero operating income and a 15% gross margin, so a $300M error is 0.2% of FY2028 revenue and nothing at the profit line. The runoff is disclosed and dated
Amortization of intangibles $300M $300M $300M The assumed path declines 20%–27% a year against a realized 20%–25%. Added back in the non-GAAP bridge, so a $100M error is $0.13 on FY2028 GAAP EPS
Stock-based compensation $850M $850M $850M Grant-date fair value per unit went from $39.62 to $102.35 to $86.52 while the stock trebled, so the declining dollar trend cannot continue at a trebled price. Added back in both the non-GAAP bridge and operating cash flow
Interest and other, net $1,400M expense — — $22.2B of fixed-rate notes at a 5.24% weighted coupon with only $3.0B of unhedged floating exposure and 100bp worth $30M. $150M of drift is under 1% of FY2028 base EPS
Effective tax rate 18% 18% 18% Dell's realized GAAP effective rate spanned 4.3% to 24.9% over FY2021–FY2026 with no trend, and the driver has a zero-width range across all scenarios. On FY2028 base pretax income of roughly $13.5B, ±300bp is ±$405M of net income, larger than the entire CSG revenue-per-unit sensitivity. The 18% is also the non-GAAP rate management guides, applied to GAAP pretax income
Diluted weighted-average shares 630M (FY2028) — — Base repurchases of $47,000M across FY2027–FY2032 take the count from 684M to 546M, which implies an average repurchase price of $237 including issuance against a market price of $464. Repeating the arithmetic at market gives roughly 618M in FY2032, worth about $2.6 of the $22.91 base FY2032 EPS
Capital expenditure, % of revenue 2.1% 2.3% 2.0% The range brackets three years of actuals, Q1 FY2027 at 2.2% and the 16-contributor consensus at 2.2%. A 20bp error is roughly $2.2B over six years against $65,126M of base cumulative free cash flow
Depreciation and amortization $3,100M — — Tangible depreciation grows because cumulative capex of roughly $22B exceeds cumulative D&A of roughly $19.9B over the six years, which reconciles the rising path with the intangible roll-off
Net working capital, % of revenue (4.0)% (1.5)% (6.0)% Net working capital was −4.9% of revenue at FY2026 year-end but −3.3% on trailing revenue at Q1 FY2027, so the latest actual is outside the base-to-bull range. The negative position is created by payables funding an AI build, so when AI revenue peaks and declines the intensity should move toward zero exactly when revenue falls. Bounds are −$4,500M to +$3,600M of cumulative cash
DFS financing receivables, % of revenue 10.0% 11.5% 8.8% The base and bull are below every year of the realized record and the bear below three of the five: 10.5%, 10.7%, 11.9%, 11.8% and 12.6% across FY2022–FY2026, with the trend rising and the 10-K attributing the FY2026 increase primarily to AI-optimized servers. The evidence supports 11.5%–12.6% with an upward bias. Holding 12.6% consumes roughly $4.7B more cumulative cash over six years, about 7% of base cumulative free cash flow, landing directly in the measure the capital-return driver is applied to
Dividend per share, FY2028 $2.77 $2.77 $2.77 Dell has never raised the dividend by 10%: the realized record is +12%, +20%, +18% and +20%, compounding at 17.5% a year. At that rate the FY2032 dividend is $6.02 against the modelled $4.06, roughly $2.8B more cash out cumulatively, which flows straight into the repurchase residual
Capital returned, % of adjusted FCF 85% 80% 90% The four-year average of 84.3% conceals annual figures of 251%, 56%, 125% and 65%, and the pattern runs opposite to the scenario logic: Dell returned the most relative to cash generated in its weakest cash years. On GAAP free cash flow Dell returned 108.5% over FY2023–FY2026
